mixed-shorthand-on-the-control-she-read.why: The exact defect the owner read in the console, on the theme toggle and the language switch, on every screen: the base set the `border` SHORTHAND and the active variant spread it and overrode the `borderColor` LONGHAND. React refuses to update a longhand on a rerender while its shorthand is set - its own words are 'can lead to styling bugs' - and on a toggle whose only visual difference IS the border, that is the control failing to show which side is on. KILLS `style-shorthand-conflict.test.ts` BY NAME, naming the pair. It kills NO Playwright test and no rendered-appearance assertion, and that is measured rather than assumed: the warning string lives in `react-dom-client.development.js` and in NO production bundle, and both style objects paint the same 1px solid border. A browser test of this PASSED ON THE BROKEN CODE before the source guard existed.

shorthand-guard-parses-nothing.why: THE NON-VACUITY FLOOR, which is the half that matters on a source guard: a parser that stops matching reports a clean nothing, and this repository has paid for that shape repeatedly. Planted, the declaration pattern matches no object and the FLOOR fails by name: 'The declaration parser found 0 style object(s), against a floor of 60.' AND THIS `why` IS CORRECTED FROM THE RUN. Its first version claimed exactly that outcome and was WRONG: the floor's first implementation counted files containing the literal ': CSSProperties = {' through a SEPARATE readFileSync, independent of the regex it was supposed to guard, so this plant applied and BOTH TESTS PASSED. The floor calls `parsedObjects` now - the same function the conflict test parses with - and a floor that does not run the thing it is a floor for is not a floor. Found by running the plant rather than by reading the guard.

console-guard-listens-after-the-navigati.why: A listener attached AFTER the navigation misses everything the first paint emitted, which is most of what a shell emits at all - so the ordering is the mechanism and not a style choice. THIS PLANT KILLS NOTHING TODAY AND IS COMMITTED SAYING SO: the shell is clean at first paint, so there is nothing for a late listener to miss, and a plant whose premise its own subject retired is recorded rather than deleted. It fails the first time the shell emits anything during its first paint - which is exactly when somebody would most want to know. The plant that DOES fail is `language-persist-left-unmocked` beside it.

language-persist-left-unmocked.why: CI CAUGHT THIS GUARD'S OWN FIXTURE, and it is the honest record of two defects of mine rather than one. `language-context.tsx` persists the preference in the background, fire-and-forget, with a `console.warn` if it fails - its own header says so: the local switch already succeeded and a remote failure is logged, never surfaced as if the switch failed. So an unmocked `PATCH /auth/me/language` makes the app warn CORRECTLY, three times. AND THE ASSERTION WAS ALSO A RACE: it SNAPSHOTTED the console, so it passed on this machine and failed on the runner purely on which side of the fetch rejection the assertion landed - with no api listening in either place. It now waits for the persist COUNT to reach its target, which only ever rises, where polling the noise array would pass on its first poll (the `toHaveCount(0)` trap). Planted, it reproduces CI's exact failure LOCALLY, which the pre-fix version could not do.
